*Tadhhalu kullu murdi'atin* (every nursing mother will be distracted): i.e., from the intensity of the terror and fear she will forget her nursing infant and be heedless of it.

*Wa tada'u kullu dhati hamlin hamlaha* (and every pregnant one will drop her burden): i.e., pregnant women will miscarry what is in their wombs from fear and fright.

*Sukara wa ma hum bi-sukara* (drunken, though they are not drunk): i.e., bewildered, having lost their reason and judgment like drunkards, though they are not drunk.

*Yujadilu fi Allahi bi-ghayri 'ilm* (dispute about God without knowledge): i.e., he says that the angels are God's daughters and that God does not give life to the dead.

*Shaytanin marid* (a rebellious devil): i.e., stripped of every good, having no good in him whatsoever.

**The meaning of the verses:**

After that divine exposition in Surah al-Anbiya', and what the Exalted has presented of the proofs of guidance and what He has made clear of the paths of salvation, the Exalted addresses a general address that includes the Arabs and non-Arabs, the disbeliever and the believer, as a warning and admonition. Indeed, its quaking, which occurs before its establishment, will cause **"every nursing mother to forget what she nursed"**, i.e., the mother will forget her child in it, **"and every pregnant one will drop her burden"**, so they will miscarry from the intensity of fear at that quaking, which announces the ruin of the universe and the annihilation of the worlds. 2. The prohibition of disputing with falsehood in order to refute and nullify the truth.
3. The prohibition of speaking about the essence and attributes of God without knowledge, whether from divine revelation or authentic prophetic speech.
4. Allying with the devils and following them leads the one who allies with and follows them to Hell and the punishment of the blazing Fire.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verse 5–7:

Explanation of the words:

*In doubt concerning the resurrection*: ar-rayb (doubt) is uncertainty accompanied by unrest and bewilderment of the soul; al-ba'th (resurrection) is life after death.

*From a drop (nutfah)*: a drop of semen emitted by the couple.

*Clinging clot ('alaqah)*: that is, a piece of congealed blood into which the drop transforms within forty days.

*Lump of flesh (mudghah)*: that is, a piece of flesh the size of what a person can chew, into which the clot transforms after forty days.

*Formed and unformed*: that is, fashioned into complete form; "formed" and "unformed" refers to the miscarriage that falls before its formation is complete.

*That We may make clear to you*: that is, Our power over what We will, and that We make you know how your creation began.

*And We cause to remain in the wombs what We will*: that is, We keep in the womb whom We will to live and remain until the end of the term of pregnancy, then We bring him out as a sound child.

*That you may reach your maturity (ashudd)*: that is, the perfection of your bodies and the completeness of your minds.

*To the most abject old age*: that is, the stage of decrepitude and senility, so that one becomes senile.

*So that he knows, after knowing, nothing*: that is, he becomes like a child in his knowledge, for he forgets everything he once knew.

*Dead (hamidah)*: lifeless, without movement, dead.

*It stirs and swells (ihtazzat wa rabat)*: that is, it moves with plants, its soil rises and it brings forth growth.

*Of every lovely kind (zawj bahij)*: that is, of every kind of plant, pleasing in appearance and beautiful.

*That is because Allah is the Truth*: that is, the true God, besides whom there is no god; so worship of Allah is truth, and worship of other than Allah is falsehood.

*And that the Hour is coming*: that is, the Resurrection.

*And that Allah will raise up those who are in the graves*: that is, He will revive them and bring them forth from their graves alive as they were before their death.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned some conditions of the Resurrection and its terrors, and disbelief in the final resurrection is what prevents people from responding to obedience and doing good, Allah called out to mankind once more to present to them the rational proofs of the resurrection, perhaps they would believe. So He said: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection﴾, that is, in uncertainty, bewilderment and inner unrest concerning the matter of people being raised alive from their graves after their death and annihilation, for their reckoning and recompense for the deeds they did in the worldly abode. Here is what removes your doubt and ends your bewilderment in this matter of faith: Allah, exalted is He, created you from dust, that is, He created your origin, your father Adam, from dust, and without doubt; then He created you from a drop, that is, the water of the man and the water of the woman, and without doubt; then from a clot after the drop transformed into it; then from a lump of flesh after the clot transformed into it, and this too is without doubt. Then the lump of flesh, if Allah wills, He transforms it into a child, fashioning it and making it a child; and if He does not will that, He does not create it and it falls from the womb, as is known and observed. Allah did this so that He might make clear to you His power, His knowledge and His good management, so that you fear Him, revere Him, love Him and obey Him. His saying: ﴿And We cause to remain in the wombs what We will for an appointed term﴾, that is, We keep that formed lump in the womb for an appointed term, which is the time of the child's birth and the end of its gestation, ﴿then We bring you forth as infants﴾, that is, as small children with neither knowledge nor forbearance; then We nurture you and raise you, by what you know of Our laws in that. ﴿Then that you may reach your maturity﴾, that is, the full growth of your bodies and minds. ﴿And among you is one who is caused to die﴾ before reaching his maturity, because divine wisdom required his death; and among you is one who lives and does not die until he is returned to the most abject old age, so he becomes decrepit and senile and becomes like a child, knowing nothing after having knowledge before his decrepitude. This is a proof of the resurrection, a rational, logical argument and a strong demonstration of people's life after their death, for He who created them from dust, then from a drop, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh necessarily implies His power to revive them after their death, since restoration is not harder than initiation.

Another rational proof is what His saying, exalted is He, contains: ﴿And you see the earth﴾, O human, ﴿lifeless (hamidah)﴾, dead, without movement or life in it; then when Allah sends down water on it from the sky, ﴿it stirs (ihtazzat)﴾, that is, it moves, ﴿and swells (rabat)﴾, that is, its soil rises and swells, and it brings forth plants of various colours, tastes and fragrances, ﴿of every lovely kind﴾, pleasing and beautiful in appearance. Is not the existence of good soil like the existence of a good womb, rainwater like the male's water, the formation of the drop in the womb like the formation of the seed in the soil, and the emergence of the crop alive and growing like the emergence of the child alive and growing; and so on, until the harvesting of the crop and the death of man? These are two rational proofs for the soundness of the final resurrection and that it is inevitably going to happen. Above all that is the information of the Creator and His notifying His creatures that He will restore them after their death; so is it of reason, logic or good taste that we should say to Him, "No, for You cannot do that"? Such a saying is filthy and rotten, which the sensible and noble of people would not wish to hear. When Allah, exalted is He, set forth these two examples, or presented these two proofs of His power, knowledge and wisdom, which require the restoration of people alive after death and annihilation for reckoning and recompense, He said, and His word is the truth: ﴿That is because Allah, He is the Truth﴾, that is, the true Lord and the true God worthy of worship, and all else is false, ﴿and that He gives life to the dead, and that He is over all things Powerful, and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that Allah will raise up those in the graves﴾. Whoever doubts should reflect on and consider the two proofs above, for he will submit to Allah, exalted is He, in what He has informed about Himself in His saying: ﴿That is because Allah, He is the Truth﴾, etc.

Guidance of the verses

1- Affirmation of the doctrine of the final resurrection and recompense for deeds on the Day of Resurrection.

2- Explanation of the stages of human creation and its indication of Allah's power, knowledge and wisdom.

3- Inference of the unseen from the perceptible present, which is the practice of sensible people, for mathematical and algebraic equations rest on the like of this.

4- Affirmation of the doctrine of monotheism, that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

2- Explanation of the stages of human creation and its indication of Allah's power, knowledge and wisdom.

3- Inference of the unseen from the perceptible present, which is the practice of sensible people, for mathematical and algebraic equations rest on the like of this.

4- Affirmation of the doctrine of monotheism, that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verse 5–7:

Explanation of the words:

*In doubt concerning the resurrection*: ar-rayb (doubt) is uncertainty accompanied by unrest and bewilderment of the soul; al-ba'th (resurrection) is life after death.

*From a drop (nutfah)*: a drop of semen emitted by the couple.

*Clinging clot ('alaqah)*: that is, a piece of congealed blood into which the drop transforms within forty days.

*Lump of flesh (mudghah)*: that is, a piece of flesh the size of what a person can chew, into which the clot transforms after forty days.

*Formed and unformed*: that is, fashioned into complete form; "formed" and "unformed" refers to the miscarriage that falls before its formation is complete.

*That We may make clear to you*: that is, Our power over what We will, and that We make you know how your creation began.

*And We cause to remain in the wombs what We will*: that is, We keep in the womb whom We will to live and remain until the end of the term of pregnancy, then We bring him out as a sound child.

*That you may reach your maturity (ashudd)*: that is, the perfection of your bodies and the completeness of your minds.

*To the most abject old age*: that is, the stage of decrepitude and senility, so that one becomes senile.

*So that he knows, after knowing, nothing*: that is, he becomes like a child in his knowledge, for he forgets everything he once knew.

*Dead (hamidah)*: lifeless, without movement, dead.

*It stirs and swells (ihtazzat wa rabat)*: that is, it moves with plants, its soil rises and it brings forth growth.

*Of every lovely kind (zawj bahij)*: that is, of every kind of plant, pleasing in appearance and beautiful.

*That is because Allah is the Truth*: that is, the true God, besides whom there is no god; so worship of Allah is truth, and worship of other than Allah is falsehood.

*And that the Hour is coming*: that is, the Resurrection.

*And that Allah will raise up those who are in the graves*: that is, He will revive them and bring them forth from their graves alive as they were before their death.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned some conditions of the Resurrection and its terrors, and disbelief in the final resurrection is what prevents people from responding to obedience and doing good, Allah called out to mankind once more to present to them the rational proofs of the resurrection, perhaps they would believe. So He said: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection﴾, that is, in uncertainty, bewilderment and inner unrest concerning the matter of people being raised alive from their graves after their death and annihilation, for their reckoning and recompense for the deeds they did in the worldly abode. Here is what removes your doubt and ends your bewilderment in this matter of faith: Allah, exalted is He, created you from dust, that is, He created your origin, your father Adam, from dust, and without doubt; then He created you from a drop, that is, the water of the man and the water of the woman, and without doubt; then from a clot after the drop transformed into it; then from a lump of flesh after the clot transformed into it, and this too is without doubt. Then the lump of flesh, if Allah wills, He transforms it into a child, fashioning it and making it a child; and if He does not will that, He does not create it and it falls from the womb, as is known and observed. Allah did this so that He might make clear to you His power, His knowledge and His good management, so that you fear Him, revere Him, love Him and obey Him. His saying: ﴿And We cause to remain in the wombs what We will for an appointed term﴾, that is, We keep that formed lump in the womb for an appointed term, which is the time of the child's birth and the end of its gestation, ﴿then We bring you forth as infants﴾, that is, as small children with neither knowledge nor forbearance; then We nurture you and raise you, by what you know of Our laws in that. ﴿Then that you may reach your maturity﴾, that is, the full growth of your bodies and minds. ﴿And among you is one who is caused to die﴾ before reaching his maturity, because divine wisdom required his death; and among you is one who lives and does not die until he is returned to the most abject old age, so he becomes decrepit and senile and becomes like a child, knowing nothing after having knowledge before his decrepitude. This is a proof of the resurrection, a rational, logical argument and a strong demonstration of people's life after their death, for He who created them from dust, then from a drop, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh necessarily implies His power to revive them after their death, since restoration is not harder than initiation.

Another rational proof is what His saying, exalted is He, contains: ﴿And you see the earth﴾, O human, ﴿lifeless (hamidah)﴾, dead, without movement or life in it; then when Allah sends down water on it from the sky, ﴿it stirs (ihtazzat)﴾, that is, it moves, ﴿and swells (rabat)﴾, that is, its soil rises and swells, and it brings forth plants of various colours, tastes and fragrances, ﴿of every lovely kind﴾, pleasing and beautiful in appearance. Is not the existence of good soil like the existence of a good womb, rainwater like the male's water, the formation of the drop in the womb like the formation of the seed in the soil, and the emergence of the crop alive and growing like the emergence of the child alive and growing; and so on, until the harvesting of the crop and the death of man? These are two rational proofs for the soundness of the final resurrection and that it is inevitably going to happen. Above all that is the information of the Creator and His notifying His creatures that He will restore them after their death; so is it of reason, logic or good taste that we should say to Him, "No, for You cannot do that"? Such a saying is filthy and rotten, which the sensible and noble of people would not wish to hear. When Allah, exalted is He, set forth these two examples, or presented these two proofs of His power, knowledge and wisdom, which require the restoration of people alive after death and annihilation for reckoning and recompense, He said, and His word is the truth: ﴿That is because Allah, He is the Truth﴾, that is, the true Lord and the true God worthy of worship, and all else is false, ﴿and that He gives life to the dead, and that He is over all things Powerful, and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that Allah will raise up those in the graves﴾. Whoever doubts should reflect on and consider the two proofs above, for he will submit to Allah, exalted is He, in what He has informed about Himself in His saying: ﴿That is because Allah, He is the Truth﴾, etc.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verse 8–13:

Explanation of the words:

"Yujadilu fi Allah" (disputes concerning Allah): that is, concerning the matter of Allah, the Exalted, attributing to Allah what is far removed from Him, such as partners, offspring, and inability to give life to the dead. This disputer was Abu Jahl.

"Bighayri 'ilm" (without knowledge): that is, without knowledge from Allah and His Messenger.

"Wa la kitabin munir" (nor a illuminating Book): that is, nor a book from the books of Allah possessing light that reveals the realities, establishes the truth, and nullifies falsehood.

"Thani 'atfihi" (turning away his side): that is, turning his neck arrogantly, for "'atf" means the side of a person.

"Lahu fi al-dunya khizy" (for him in this world is disgrace): Allah made him taste it on the Day of Badr, when he was slaughtered there and his head was cut off.

"Bizalamin lil-'abid" (by wrongdoing to the servants): that is, by One who is wrongful to the servants, so that He punishes them without any wrongdoing on their part against themselves.

"Ya'budu Allah 'ala harf" (worships Allah on an edge): that is, in doubt about Islam, whether it is true or false, because of their ignorance of it. Most of these were Bedouin Arabs.

"Ituma'anna bihi" (he is content with it): that is, his soul settles into Islam and is pleased with it.

"Wa in asabathu fitnah" (but if a trial befalls him): that is, a test through loss of wealth, illness in the body, or the like.

"Inqalaba 'ala wajhihi" (he turns back on his face): that is, he turns back from Islam to the pre-Islamic disbelief he was upon.

"Ma la yadurruhu wa la yanfa'uhu" (what neither harms him nor benefits him): that is, an idol that does not harm him if he does not worship it, nor benefit him if he worships it.

"La-bi'sa al-mawla" (evil is the protector): that is, how wretched is this helper as a helper.

"Wa la-bi'sa al-'ashir" (and evil is the companion): that is, the one who associates, the constant companion.

Explanation of the verses:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And among people is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge﴾ This is a second person, joined to the first mentioned in His words: ﴿And among people is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil﴾ [al-Hajj: 3]. He is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, one of the leaders of the strife in Makkah. This person is the Pharaoh of this nation, 'Amr ibn Hisham, known as Abu Jahl. Allah speaks of him, saying: ﴿And among people is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book﴾. Rather, he disputes with ignorance, and how ugly is the dispute of ignorance and of the ignorant. He disputes concerning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. How strange! Does he want to establish for Allah the Exalted a son, a daughter, incapacity, partners, and intercessors, while he has no knowledge from revelation, nor from any divine Book revealed to any of His prophets?

His words: ﴿Turning away his side﴾ describe him in his manner of walking, dragging his garment, turning his cheek, leaning to one of his sides out of arrogance and conceit. His disputing is not for seeking guidance, nor merely for love of victory for himself, but to lead others astray from the path of Allah, the Exalted, which is Islam, so that they do not enter it, and thus they would be complete and happy in it in both lives.

His words: ﴿For him in this world is disgrace﴾ meaning humiliation and degradation. He received it when he was killed at Badr in the worst manner: his head was cut off and separated from his body, and those whom he used to mock and torment from among the weak believers took their revenge upon him.

His words: ﴿And We will make him taste the punishment of the burning on the Day of Resurrection﴾. Allah made him taste it immediately when he was killed, for his soul is in the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection he will enter it with his body and soul.

His words: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward﴾ meaning it will be said to him on the Day of Resurrection: that disgrace and humiliation and the punishment of the burning are for what your hands have sent forward of polytheism, wrongdoing, and sins. ﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, and you are among them. By Allah, He did not wrong you; rather you wronged yourself, and Allah is far exalted above injustice because of His perfect power and self-sufficiency.

His words: ﴿And among people is he who worships Allah on an edge﴾ meaning in doubt. This is a third person, joined to the two before him: the person of some Bedouins who entered Islam not out of knowledge and conviction, but out of doubt and greed, and this is the meaning of "on an edge." If good befalls them of wealth, health, and well-being, they are content with Islam, their souls settle, and they persist in it. But if a trial befalls them, that is a test in themselves, wealth, or children, they turn back on their faces, meaning they apostatize from Islam and return from it, and by that they lose both this world and the next. They gain neither this world nor do they succeed in the Hereafter. Allah said: ﴿That is the manifest loss﴾, meaning the clear and evident loss, for had they remained upon Islam they would have succeeded in the Hereafter, and Allah would have replaced for them what they lost of wealth or self.

His words: ﴿He calls upon, besides Allah, that which neither harms him nor benefits him﴾ meaning that apostate who has turned back on his face calls upon an idol that does not harm him if he abandons its worship, and does not benefit him if he worships it. His words: ﴿That is the far-off error﴾ meaning the calling upon and worship of what neither harms nor benefits is error away from guidance, goodness, success, and profit, and it is also far off, for its adherent may never return or be guided.

And His words: ﴿He calls upon one whose harm is nearer than his benefit﴾ meaning that apostate from monotheism who calls to polytheism: the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit on the Day of Resurrection, for he may disown him and be gathered with him in Hell, so that both become fuel for it. Allah said: ﴿Wretched is the protector, and wretched is the companion﴾, the associate and constant companion. Thus Allah censures and denounces what the polytheists used to hope for from them and expect their intercession on the Day of Resurrection, as a warning to them against polytheism and the worship of other than Him, glorified and exalted.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The ugliness of the ignorant person disputing about what he has no knowledge of.

2- The condemnation of arrogance and conceit, whether from a disbeliever or a believer.

3- The uselessness of worship whose performer doubts its benefit and does not believe in its obligation and legitimacy.

4- Religion is not valid with doubt.

5- Affirmation of monotheism and denunciation of polytheism and polytheists.

He is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, one of the leaders of the strife in Makkah. This person is the Pharaoh of this nation, 'Amr ibn Hisham, known as Abu Jahl. Allah speaks of him, saying: ﴿And among people is he who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book﴾. Rather, he disputes with ignorance, and how ugly is the dispute of ignorance and of the ignorant. He disputes concerning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. How strange! Does he want to establish for Allah the Exalted a son, a daughter, incapacity, partners, and intercessors, while he has no knowledge from revelation, nor from any divine Book revealed to any of His prophets?

His words: ﴿Turning away his side﴾ describe him in his manner of walking, dragging his garment, turning his cheek, leaning to one of his sides out of arrogance and conceit. His disputing is not for seeking guidance, nor merely for love of victory for himself, but to lead others astray from the path of Allah, the Exalted, which is Islam, so that they do not enter it, and thus they would be complete and happy in it in both lives.

His words: ﴿For him in this world is disgrace﴾ meaning humiliation and degradation. He received it when he was killed at Badr in the worst manner: his head was cut off and separated from his body, and those whom he used to mock and torment from among the weak believers took their revenge upon him.

His words: ﴿And We will make him taste the punishment of the burning on the Day of Resurrection﴾. Allah made him taste it immediately when he was killed, for his soul is in the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection he will enter it with his body and soul.

His words: ﴿That is for what your hands have put forward﴾ meaning it will be said to him on the Day of Resurrection: that disgrace and humiliation and the punishment of the burning are for what your hands have sent forward of polytheism, wrongdoing, and sins. ﴿And that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, and you are among them. By Allah, He did not wrong you; rather you wronged yourself, and Allah is far exalted above injustice because of His perfect power and self-sufficiency.

His words: ﴿And among people is he who worships Allah on an edge﴾ meaning in doubt. This is a third person, joined to the two before him: the person of some Bedouins who entered Islam not out of knowledge and conviction, but out of doubt and greed, and this is the meaning of "on an edge." If good befalls them of wealth, health, and well-being, they are content with Islam, their souls settle, and they persist in it. But if a trial befalls them, that is a test in themselves, wealth, or children, they turn back on their faces, meaning they apostatize from Islam and return from it, and by that they lose both this world and the next. They gain neither this world nor do they succeed in the Hereafter. Allah said: ﴿That is the manifest loss﴾, meaning the clear and evident loss, for had they remained upon Islam they would have succeeded in the Hereafter, and Allah would have replaced for them what they lost of wealth or self.

His words: ﴿He calls upon, besides Allah, that which neither harms him nor benefits him﴾ meaning that apostate who has turned back on his face calls upon an idol that does not harm him if he abandons its worship, and does not benefit him if he worships it. His words: ﴿That is the far-off error﴾ meaning the calling upon and worship of what neither harms nor benefits is error away from guidance, goodness, success, and profit, and it is also far off, for its adherent may never return or be guided.

And His words: ﴿He calls upon one whose harm is nearer than his benefit﴾ meaning that apostate from monotheism who calls to polytheism: the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit on the Day of Resurrection, for he may disown him and be gathered with him in Hell, so that both become fuel for it. Allah said: ﴿Wretched is the protector, and wretched is the companion﴾, the associate and constant companion. Thus Allah censures and denounces what the polytheists used to hope for from them and expect their intercession on the Day of Resurrection, as a warning to them against polytheism and the worship of other than Him, glorified and exalted.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The ugliness of the ignorant person disputing about what he has no knowledge of.

2- The condemnation of arrogance and conceit, whether from a disbeliever or a believer.

3- The uselessness of worship whose performer doubts its benefit and does not believe in its obligation and legitimacy.

4- Religion is not valid with doubt.

5- Affirmation of monotheism and denunciation of polytheism and polytheists.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verse 8–13:

Explanation of the words:

"Yujadilu fi Allah" (disputes concerning Allah): that is, concerning the matter of Allah, the Exalted, attributing to Allah what is far removed from Him, such as partners, offspring, and inability to give life to the dead. This disputer was Abu Jahl.

"Bighayri 'ilm" (without knowledge): that is, without knowledge from Allah and His Messenger.

"Wa la kitabin munir" (nor a illuminating Book): that is, nor a book from the books of Allah possessing light that reveals the realities, establishes the truth, and nullifies falsehood.

"Thani 'atfihi" (turning away his side): that is, turning his neck arrogantly, for "'atf" means the side of a person.

"Lahu fi al-dunya khizy" (for him in this world is disgrace): Allah made him taste it on the Day of Badr, when he was slaughtered there and his head was cut off.

"Bizalamin lil-'abid" (by wrongdoing to the servants): that is, by One who is wrongful to the servants, so that He punishes them without any wrongdoing on their part against themselves.

"Ya'budu Allah 'ala harf" (worships Allah on an edge): that is, in doubt about Islam, whether it is true or false, because of their ignorance of it. Most of these were Bedouin Arabs.

"Ituma'anna bihi" (he is content with it): that is, his soul settles into Islam and is pleased with it.

"Wa in asabathu fitnah" (but if a trial befalls him): that is, a test through loss of wealth, illness in the body, or the like.

"Inqalaba 'ala wajhihi" (he turns back on his face): that is, he turns back from Islam to the pre-Islamic disbelief he was upon.

"Ma la yadurruhu wa la yanfa'uhu" (what neither harms him nor benefits him): that is, an idol that does not harm him if he does not worship it, nor benefit him if he worships it.

"La-bi'sa al-mawla" (evil is the protector): that is, how wretched is this helper as a helper.

"Wa la-bi'sa al-'ashir" (and evil is the companion): that is, the one who associates, the constant companion.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verse 14–17:

Explanation of the words:

Wa 'amilu al-salihat: that is, the obligatory duties (fara'id) and voluntary acts (nawafil) and deeds of goodness.

Yaf'alu ma yurid: such as honouring the obedient and humiliating the disobedient, and other things, such as showing mercy to the believer and punishing the disbeliever.

An lan yansurahu Allah: that is, Muhammad (ﷺ).

Falyamdud bi sabab: that is, with a rope.

Ila al-sama': that is, to the roof (saqf) between him and it.

Wa-liyakhtaniq ghayzan: and let him choke with rage.

Hal yadhhabanna kayduhu: that is, in not helping the Prophet (ﷺ), which enrages him.

Wa-kadhalika anzalnahu: that is, and in the same way as Our sending down those previous signs, We sent down the Qur'an.

Hadu: that is, the Jews.

Wa-al-sabi'in: a sect of the Christians.

Wa-al-majus: worshippers of fire and the stars.

Ala kulli shay' shahid: that is, Knowing of it and Preserver of it.

The meaning of the verses:

After Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the recompense of the disbelievers and those who waver between disbelief and faith, He informed that He admits those who believe in Him, His Messenger, the meeting with their Lord, and His promise and threat, and who do righteous deeds, which are the obligatory duties that Allah has enjoined upon them and the voluntary acts that He encouraged them to perform, admitting them, as a reward for their faith and good deeds, into gardens beneath which rivers flow. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does whatever He wills﴾, among which is His punishing whoever disbelieves in Him and disobeys Him, and His mercy toward whoever believes in Him and obeys Him. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever thinks that Allah will not support him﴾, that is, whoever thinks that Allah will not support His Messenger, His religion, and His believing servants, so he wavers and does not believe and does not join the ranks of the Muslims, like the Banu Asad and Ghatafan. We guide him to what would remove his rage, since it grieves him that Allah supports His Messenger, His Book, His religion, and His believing servants: let him bring a rope and tie it to a beam in the ceiling of his house, and pull it around his neck, then let him cut the rope, and see, after this suicidal act, whether his scheme removes what enrages him.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have sent it down as clear signs﴾, that is, and in the same manner as that sending down of the signs mentioned earlier, which show Allah's power and knowledge in creation, the reviving of the earth, and the restoring of life after death, We sent down the Qur'an as clear signs bearing guidance and good for whoever believes in them and acts upon the laws and rulings within them. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that Allah guides whom He wills﴾, that is, His guidance is by enabling him to reflect and contemplate, so he recognises the truth, seeks it, and adopts it in belief, speech, and action.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believe﴾, who are the Muslims, ﴿and those who are Jews﴾, who are the Jews, ﴿and the Sabians﴾, who are a sect of the Christians who read the Psalms and worship the stars, ﴿and the Christians﴾, who are the worshippers of the cross, ﴿and the Magians﴾, who are the worshippers of fire and the stars, ﴿and those who associate others with Allah﴾, who are the worshippers of idols: all of these, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection, admitting the believers into Paradise and admitting the people of those false creeds into the Fire. This is the true decision. The religions are six: one religion for the Most Merciful and five for Satan. The people of the religion of the Most Merciful, He admits them into His mercy, and the people of the religion of Satan, He admits them into the Fire with Satan. His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Witness over all things﴾, that is, Knowing of everything, nothing is hidden from Him, and He will recompense every doer for what he has done. None perishes before Allah except one who is destined to perish. He has sent down His Book, sent His Messenger, encouraged and warned, promised and threatened, and people choose what has been decreed for them or against them. Glory be to Allah, the Mighty.

Guidance from the verses:

1- All religions other than Islam derive from the inspiration of Satan, and their adherents are losers, except Islam, which is the true religion of Allah, and its adherents are the victorious; its adherents are those who uphold it in belief, worship, judgement, and rule.

2- Indeed Allah supports His religion and honours its adherents; whoever is enraged by this and is not pleased, let him choke.

3- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.

4- Affirmation of Allah's will and purpose: He, exalted is He, does what He wills and guides whom He wills.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 22, Verse 18**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Alam tara*: Have you not seen, that is, have you not seen with your heart so that you know?

*Yasjudu lahu*: Yakhdau wa yadhillu lahu, that is, submits and humbles himself before Him by placing his face on the ground before the Lord, exalted is He. (*Sujud*, prostration, here means this act of submission.)

*Man fi as-samawat*: from among the angels.

*Wa ad-dawabb*: from among all the animals that crawl upon the earth.

*Haqqa 'alayhi al-'adhab*: the punishment has become due for him, so it is certain that it will befall him.

*Wa man yuhini Allah*: that is, He wretches him into a humiliating punishment.

*Fa-ma lahu min mukrim*: that is, he has no honorer, meaning no one who makes him happy, and Allah has made him wretched.

**The meaning of the noble verse:**

The Exalted says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Have you not seen﴾, O Messenger, with your heart so that you know, ﴿that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens﴾ from among the angels, ﴿and whoever is on the earth﴾ from among the jinn and the animals, ﴿and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures, and many of mankind﴾, who are the obedient believers. "And many" means that, from among mankind, ﴿the punishment has become due for them﴾, that is, punishment has become obligatory and established for them. The prostration here is not the prostration of worship and drawing near that we perform, but the prostration of submission: their shadows prostrate to Him in the mornings and evenings.

As for His words: ﴿And whoever Allah humiliates, for him there is no honorer﴾, that means whoever Allah wills to make wretched and punish, there is no one to honor him by removing the punishment from him and making him happy in the abode of happiness.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does what He wills﴾. So whoever He wills He humiliates, and whoever He wills He honors. The creation is His creation, and He has absolute authority over them. Whoever He wills He makes mighty, and whoever He wills He makes low. Therefore His servants must turn back to Him in repentance, seeking His mercy and fearing His punishment, for this is the surest way to be saved from His punishment and the closest to His mercy.

**Lessons (Hidayah) of the noble verse:**

1. Affirmation of Allah's lordship and divinity.
2. The prostration (*sujud*) of created things according to their natures and what Allah intended for them.
3. Everything submits to Allah except man, and most individuals among mankind are disobedient to Him and rebellious against Him, and by that they deserve the humiliating punishment.
4. The one who recites this verse, and the one who hears its recitation, is recommended to prostrate to Allah when they reach His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does what He wills﴾.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 19–24:

Explanation of the words:

Khasmān (two adversaries): a believing adversary and a disbelieving adversary, each wanting to win against his opponent.

Ikhtaṣamū fī rabbihim (they dispute concerning their Lord): that is, concerning His religion.

Quṭṭiʿat lahum thiyāb (garments have been cut out for them): that is, garments have been tailored for them to fit the measure of their bodies.

Yuṣhharu bihi mā fī buṭūnihim (whereby what is in their bellies is melted): that is, it is melted by the ḥamīm, which is hot water, [mixed] with fats and other things.

Maqāmiʿ min ḥadīd (rods of iron): plural of miqmaʿah, an iron implement like a shield.

Wadhūqū ʿadhāb al-ḥarīq (and taste the punishment of the burning): that is, it will be said to them as rebuke and reproach: taste the punishment of the Fire.

Lu'lu'an (pearls): that is, bracelets of pearls adorned with gold.

Ilā al-ṭayyib min al-qawl (to the good of speech): this is the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

Ilā ṣirāṭ al-ḥamīd (to the path of the Praiseworthy): that is, to Islam, for it is the path of Allah that leads to His pleasure and His Paradise.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿These two adversaries﴾ — the first adversary is the Muslims, and the second is the people of polytheism and disbelief. ﴿dispute concerning their Lord﴾, that is, concerning His religion: each adversary claims to be upon the true religion, and they died upon that, and Allah the Exalted will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿As for those who disbelieved﴾, who are the people of false religion, they will enter the Fire, and garments of fire will be cut out for them. ﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads﴾, that is, water that has reached the utmost of heat, ﴿whereby what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted﴾, [namely] flesh and fat. ﴿And for them are rods of iron﴾ with which they are beaten. ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it﴾, that is, out of the Fire, because of the great distress that overtakes them, ﴿they will be returned to it﴾, that is, the guardians of Hell will compel them to return into it and will not permit them to come out of it. They will be told: ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾, that is, do not come out of it, and taste the punishment of the burning. This is the recompense of the disbelieving adversary. As for the believing adversary, this is his recompense, which is in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believed and did righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾, that is, bracelets of pearls adorned with gold. ﴿And their clothing therein﴾, that is, in Paradise, ﴿is silk﴾. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they are guided to good speech﴾ in this world, which is "there is no god but Allah," and the rest of the remembrances and glorifications and every good speech. ﴿And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴾, and this is the path that leads to the pleasure of their Lord, which is Islam. All of this is by the success granted by their Lord, in whom and in whose Messenger they believed, and whom they obeyed by doing what He loves and abandoning what displeases Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Establishing the reality that the believer is an adversary of the disbeliever and the disbeliever is an adversary of the believer in every time and place, since the verse was revealed concerning ʿAlī, Ḥamzah and ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith as the believing adversaries, and ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah as the disbelieving adversary; they fought one another at Badr in single combat, and Allah granted victory to the believing adversary over the disbeliever.

2. Explanation of the recompense of each of the disbelievers and the believers in the Hereafter.

3. Affirmation of the creed of resurrection and recompense by mentioning the conditions of the Hereafter and what people will have there.

4. Explanation of the good speech, which is the word of tawḥīd and the remembrance of Allah the Exalted.

5. Explanation of the path of the Praiseworthy, which is Islam; may Allah make us among its people.

Ikhtaṣamū fī rabbihim (they dispute concerning their Lord): that is, concerning His religion.

Quṭṭiʿat lahum thiyāb (garments have been cut out for them): that is, garments have been tailored for them to fit the measure of their bodies.

Yuṣhharu bihi mā fī buṭūnihim (whereby what is in their bellies is melted): that is, it is melted by the ḥamīm, which is hot water, [mixed] with fats and other things.

Maqāmiʿ min ḥadīd (rods of iron): plural of miqmaʿah, an iron implement like a shield.

Wadhūqū ʿadhāb al-ḥarīq (and taste the punishment of the burning): that is, it will be said to them as rebuke and reproach: taste the punishment of the Fire.

Lu'lu'an (pearls): that is, bracelets of pearls adorned with gold.

Ilā al-ṭayyib min al-qawl (to the good of speech): this is the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

Ilā ṣirāṭ al-ḥamīd (to the path of the Praiseworthy): that is, to Islam, for it is the path of Allah that leads to His pleasure and His Paradise.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿These two adversaries﴾ — the first adversary is the Muslims, and the second is the people of polytheism and disbelief. ﴿dispute concerning their Lord﴾, that is, concerning His religion: each adversary claims to be upon the true religion, and they died upon that, and Allah the Exalted will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿As for those who disbelieved﴾, who are the people of false religion, they will enter the Fire, and garments of fire will be cut out for them. ﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads﴾, that is, water that has reached the utmost of heat, ﴿whereby what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted﴾, [namely] flesh and fat. ﴿And for them are rods of iron﴾ with which they are beaten. ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it﴾, that is, out of the Fire, because of the great distress that overtakes them, ﴿they will be returned to it﴾, that is, the guardians of Hell will compel them to return into it and will not permit them to come out of it. They will be told: ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾, that is, do not come out of it, and taste the punishment of the burning. This is the recompense of the disbelieving adversary. As for the believing adversary, this is his recompense, which is in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believed and did righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾, that is, bracelets of pearls adorned with gold. ﴿And their clothing therein﴾, that is, in Paradise, ﴿is silk﴾. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they are guided to good speech﴾ in this world, which is "there is no god but Allah," and the rest of the remembrances and glorifications and every good speech. ﴿And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴾, and this is the path that leads to the pleasure of their Lord, which is Islam. All of this is by the success granted by their Lord, in whom and in whose Messenger they believed, and whom they obeyed by doing what He loves and abandoning what displeases Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Establishing the reality that the believer is an adversary of the disbeliever and the disbeliever is an adversary of the believer in every time and place, since the verse was revealed concerning ʿAlī, Ḥamzah and ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith as the believing adversaries, and ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah as the disbelieving adversary; they fought one another at Badr in single combat, and Allah granted victory to the believing adversary over the disbeliever.

2. Explanation of the recompense of each of the disbelievers and the believers in the Hereafter.

3. Affirmation of the creed of resurrection and recompense by mentioning the conditions of the Hereafter and what people will have there.

4. Explanation of the good speech, which is the word of tawḥīd and the remembrance of Allah the Exalted.

5. Explanation of the path of the Praiseworthy, which is Islam; may Allah make us among its people.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verse 25:

Explanation of the words:

Kafaru (disbelieved): they denied the Oneness of God, denied His Messenger, and denied what had come to them from their Lord.

Wa yasudduna 'an sabil Allah (and they bar from the way of God): they prevent people from entering Islam and turn them away from it.

Al-Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque): Mecca, the honoured city, with the Sacred Mosque included within it.

Al-'Akif (the one who resides): the one who lives in Mecca for worship in the Sacred Mosque.

Al-Bad (the visitor): the one who comes to Mecca from elsewhere and travels to it.

Bi-ilhad bi-zulm (with deviation through injustice): i.e., ilhad, meaning a deviation from the truth, accompanied by injustice to oneself or to others.

Meaning of the noble verse:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God﴾. This noble verse carries a threat and a severe warning to everyone who disbelieves in the Oneness of God, denies His Messenger and what he brought of guidance and the true religion, and bars from the way of God, that is, turns people away from entering Islam, and from entering the Sacred Mosque to circumambulate the House and to reside in Mecca for worship in the Sacred Mosque. Although the verse addresses the polytheists who barred the Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions from entering Mecca in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, it is general in application to everyone who disbelieves and bars, until the Day of Resurrection. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That which We have made for people, equal are the resident therein and the visitor﴾ is a description of the Sacred Mosque, for God, exalted is He, made it a place of worship for everyone who comes to it and stays there, or comes to it for worship and then leaves it. The resident therein, that is, the one who dwells in it, and the visitor who has just arrived, are equal in their right to reside in Mecca and the Sacred Mosque for worship.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation through injustice﴾ means: whoever intends, i.e., resolves, to deviate from the truth therein by committing an injustice, such as polytheism and all other sins and disobediences, whether those that are confined to the doer or those that extend to others. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We will make him taste of a painful punishment﴾ is the recompense for whoever disbelieves and bars from the way of God and the Sacred Mosque, and for whoever intends therein deviation through injustice to himself or to others.

Guidance of the noble verse

From the guidance of the noble verse:

1- The condemnation of disbelief, of barring from the way of God and from the Sacred Mosque, and of injustice therein, and the severe warning to the one who commits these.

2- Mecca is the city of God and His sanctuary. It is the right of every Muslim to reside there for worship and devotion, so long as he does not commit injustice and violate the sanctity of the Haram through sins and disobediences, especially polytheism, injustice, and error.

3- The great standing of the Haram, for one is held to account there merely for the resolve to act, even if he does not act.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verse 26–29:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And when We settled for Abraham the place of the House﴾: that is, remember, O our Messenger, when We settled Abraham at Makkah, showing him the location of the House.

﴿that you associate not anything with Me﴾: that is, We enjoined upon him that he not associate anything with Me, of shirk and partners.

﴿And purify My House﴾: cleanse My House from the filth of shirk and the impurities of the polytheists.

﴿And proclaim to mankind the Hajj﴾: announce among the people with your highest voice.

﴿on foot and on every lean camel﴾: on foot and riding upon lean she-camels.

﴿from every deep ravine﴾: a wide road, far-reaching in the depths of the earth's regions.

﴿on known days﴾: these are the days of at-Tashriq (the days of tashriq, the 11th–13th of Dhul-Hijjah).

﴿of the beasts of cattle﴾: that is, camels, cows and sheep, since the hady (sacrificial offering) is not valid except from them.

﴿the poor, the needy﴾: that is, the one who is severely poor.

﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾: that is, let them remove their dirt that accumulated over the period of ihram.

﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾: that is, by slaughtering and sacrificing what they vowed to Allah of offerings and sacrificial animals.

Meaning of the verses:

His Exalted saying: ﴿And when We settled for Abraham the place of the House﴾ means: remember, O our Messenger, to your people who falsely and baselessly claim affiliation with Abraham, though he was a monotheist while they are polytheists. Tell them how his Lord settled him at the place of the House to build it and raise its structure, and how Allah made a covenant with him and charged him to purify it from sensory filth such as blood and dirt, and from the immaterial filth such as shirk, sins and all other wrongdoings. This was for the sake of those who circumambulate it, those who stand in prayer, and those who bow and prostrate within it, since ruka' is the plural of raki' and sujud is the plural of saajid, so that they are not harmed by any harm, immaterial or physical, while they are around the House of their Lord, in its land and its sanctuary. Let your people remember this, while they have set up idols and statues around the House, fight everyone who says "There is no god but Allah," have barred you and your companions from the Sacred Mosque, and prevented you from circumambulating the Ancient House. Where then have their minds gone, when they claim to be upon the religion of Abraham and Ishmael? This is what His Exalted saying indicates: ﴿And when We settled for Abraham the place of the House, [saying], "Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate."﴾

His Exalted saying ﴿And proclaim to mankind the Hajj﴾ means: We made a covenant with him, commanding him to call out among the people that he should proclaim and announce: "O people, indeed your Lord has built for you a House, so perform Hajj to it." He did so, and Allah made his voice heard by whomever He willed among His servants, those for whom it had been decreed from eternity that they would perform Hajj, and He made their path easy. They have performed Hajj in fact, and to Allah belongs praise and grace.

His Exalted saying: ﴿they will come to you on foot﴾ means: upon you is the calling, and upon Us is the delivering, so call out. ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾, that is, walking, ﴿and on every lean camel﴾ from the emaciated she-camels, ﴿coming from every deep ravine﴾, that is, a distant road in the depths and far reaches of the earth, such as Andalusia in the west and Indonesia in the east. His Exalted saying: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾ means: they come to you to witness benefits for themselves, religious ones such as the forgiveness of their sins, the answering of their supplications, attaining the pleasure of their Lord, and learning their religion from their scholars, and worldly ones such as profit from trade through buying and selling, offering goods, and various kinds of crafts. His Exalted saying: ﴿and mention the name of Allah﴾ means thanking Allah for His blessings and bounty upon them, and that is throughout the days of Hajj, from the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah until the end of the days of at-Tashriq, through prayer, remembrance and supplication, as they mention the name of Allah over what He has provided them of the beasts of cattle, at the slaughtering of camels and the sacrificing of cows and sheep, by the slaughterer or sacrificer saying "In the name of Allah, Allah is the greatest." His Exalted saying: ﴿So eat from them﴾ means: from the beasts of cattle that you have slaughtered or sacrificed seeking nearness to Us, such as the hady of tamattu' or voluntary offerings. ﴿And feed the miserable one, the poor﴾, who is the one whose poverty is severe. His Exalted saying: ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾ means by removing the disarray and dirt that clung to them throughout the period of ihram.

His saying: ﴿and let them fulfil their vows﴾ means: whoever among them has vowed an offering to be slaughtered in the Sacred Precinct, let him fulfil that, since this is the time for fulfilling what he vowed to sacrifice or slaughter in the Sacred Precinct. His saying ﴿and let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾ means: and let them perform the Tawaf al-Ifadah, which is a pillar of Hajj and is not valid except after standing at 'Arafah and throwing the Jamrat al-'Aqabah on the morning of the 'Eid, the 'Eid al-Adha.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to build the House and rebuild it whenever it collapses or is destroyed, and the obligation to purify it from everything that harms those who circumambulate and those who stay in the Sacred Mosque, including shirk, sins and all other wrongdoings, and from filth such as urine, blood and the like.

2- The legitimacy of opening offices to promote Hajj.

3- The permissibility of trade during one's stay for Hajj.

4- The obligation to thank Allah and remember Him.

5- The permissibility of eating from the hady and from voluntary sacrifices, indeed its recommendation.

6- The obligation of shaving or shortening the hair after throwing the Jamrat al-'Aqabah.

7- The obligation to fulfil lawful vows; as for vows made to saints, they are shirk and it is not permissible to fulfil them.

8- The establishment of Tawaf al-Ifadah and clarification of its time, which is after standing at 'Arafah and throwing the Jamrat al-'Aqabah.

﴿And purify My House﴾: cleanse My House from the filth of shirk and the impurities of the polytheists.

﴿And proclaim to mankind the Hajj﴾: announce among the people with your highest voice.

﴿on foot and on every lean camel﴾: on foot and riding upon lean she-camels.

﴿from every deep ravine﴾: a wide road, far-reaching in the depths of the earth's regions.

﴿on known days﴾: these are the days of at-Tashriq (the days of tashriq, the 11th–13th of Dhul-Hijjah).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 30–33:

Explanation of the words:

Dhalika (that): i.e., the matter is this, like the speech of one who says "this is what I mentioned... and so-and-so..."

Hurumat Allah (the sacred things of Allah): plural of hurma, that which Allah has forbidden to violate, whether by speech or action.

Fa-huwa khayrun lahu 'inda rabbihi (it is better for him with his Lord): i.e., it is better for him in the Hereafter for the one who venerates the sacred things of Allah and does not violate them.

Illa ma yutla 'alaykum (except what is recited to you): i.e., its prohibition, namely carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah.

Fa-ijtanibu al-rijs (so avoid the abomination): i.e., avoid the worship of idols.

Wa-ijtanibu qawl al-zur (and avoid the word of falsehood): it is lying, and the greatest lying is that which is about Allah, the Most High, as well as shirk and false testimony.

Hunafa' lillah (upright to Allah): monotheists devoted to Him, turning away from every religion to Islam.

Kharra min al-sama' (he falls from the sky): i.e., he falls.

Fa-takhtafahu al-tayr (so the birds snatch him): i.e., they seize him swiftly.

Sha'a'ir Allah (the symbols of Allah): the markers of His religion, and here they are the camels (budn), by choosing the good, fat ones among them.

Fa-innaha min taqwa al-qulub (for it is from the piety of hearts): i.e., their veneration arises from the piety of their hearts.

Lakum fiha manafi' (for you in them are benefits): among them, riding them and carrying upon them what does not harm them, and drinking their milk.

Ila ajal musamma (until a specified term): i.e., a set time, which is their slaughter at the Sacred Precinct during the days of tashriq.

Thumma mahilluha ila al-bayt al-'atiq (then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House): i.e., near the Ancient House, which is Mecca and the Sacred Precinct.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the rites of Hajj. Allah, the Most High, says ﴿That [is so]﴾, i.e., the matter is that which you have learned: the completion of the rites (qada' al-tafath), namely removing hair from the head, trimming the moustache, clipping the nails, changing garments, and slaughtering and sacrificing the offerings and sacrificial animals. ﴿And whoever honours the sacred things of Allah﴾ among you ﴿- then it is better for him with his Lord﴾, i.e., that honouring of them, by respecting them and not violating them, is better for him with his Lord on the day he meets Him. Allah, the Most High, says: ﴿And the grazing livestock has been made lawful for you﴾, i.e., camels, cattle and sheep, which Allah, the Most High, has made lawful for you to eat and to benefit from. Allah, the Most High, says: ﴿except what is recited to you﴾ concerning its prohibition, as came in Surahs al-Baqarah, al-Ma'idah and al-An'am, among it His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that over which other than Allah has been invoked, the strangled, the beaten, the fallen, the gored, and what a wild beast has eaten, except what you have slaughtered, and what is sacrificed on stone altars﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3]. And His saying: ﴿So avoid the abomination of idols﴾, i.e., avoid the worship of idols, for they are an abomination, so do not draw near to them in worship or otherwise, out of zeal for Allah and disapproval of them and of worshipping them. And His saying: ﴿and avoid the word of falsehood﴾, which is lying in every form, and false testimony. The greatest lying is that which is about Allah by ascribing to Him what is exempt from Him, or attributing to Him something such as a son or a partner, from which He is exempt, or describing Him with incapacity or any deficiency. And His saying: ﴿upright to Allah, not associating others with Him﴾, i.e., monotheists in His essence, attributes and acts of worship, turning away from all religions to His religion, Islam, not associating with Him any kind of shirk or partners. And His saying, Most High: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah﴾ by worshipping another god or directing to him some of the acts of worship that belong to Allah, the Most High, then his state in loss and ruin is the ruin of one who has fallen from the sky, i.e., has fallen from it after being raised up to it, ﴿and the birds snatch him﴾, i.e., seize him swiftly and tear him to pieces as falcons and eagles do to small birds, ﴿or the wind throws him into a remote place﴾ far away, so that he is never found again. Thus he is between two states: either the birds snatch him or the wind hurls him down, and he is a loser and destroyed. This is the state of one who associates others with Allah, the Most High, worshipping another alongside Him, after he was in the heaven of purity and spiritual serenity through the soundness of his nature and the goodness of his soul; then he was overturned into the mire of shirk, we seek Allah's refuge. And His saying, Most High: ﴿That [is so]. And whoever honours the symbols of Allah - indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾, i.e., the matter is that: the veneration of the sacred things of Allah, avoiding the word of falsehood and shirk, and the explanation of the loss of the polytheist; and whoever honours the symbols of Allah, which are the markers of His religion among all the rites, especially the camels that are brought as offerings to the Sacred Precinct. Their veneration through choosing them for goodness and fatness arises from the piety of hearts. Whoever honours them in obedience to Allah and drawing near to Him, that indicates the piety of his heart toward his Lord, Most High. The Messenger (ﷺ) pointed to his chest and said: "Piety is here, piety is here, piety is here," three times. And His saying, Most High: ﴿For you in them are benefits until a specified term﴾, i.e., Allah, the Most High, has permitted the believers to benefit from the offerings while they drive them to the Sacred Precinct, by riding them, carrying upon them what does not harm them, and drinking from their milk. And His saying, Most High: ﴿Then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾, i.e., their place of sacrifice is near the Ancient House, which is the Sacred Precinct, where they are slaughtered if they are of those that are slaughtered, or sacrificed if they are of those that are sacrificed.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation to honour the sacred things of Allah, for in them is great good.

2- Confirmation of the lawfulness of grazing livestock on condition that the name of Allah is mentioned when they are slaughtered or sacrificed.

3- The prohibition of falsehood and false testimony, and it is related that false testimony was equated with shirk with Allah.

4- The obligation to abandon the worship of idols, to keep away from them, and to abandon everything that is connected to them.

5- The explanation of the punishment of shirk and the loss of the polytheist.

6- Honouring the symbols of Allah, especially the offering camels, arises from the piety of their owners' hearts.

7- The permissibility of benefiting from the offering camels by riding them, drinking their milk, and carrying upon them, up to the point of their slaughter at the Sacred Precinct.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 30–33:

Explanation of the words:

Dhalika (that): i.e., the matter is this, like the speech of one who says "this is what I mentioned... and so-and-so..."

Hurumat Allah (the sacred things of Allah): plural of hurma, that which Allah has forbidden to violate, whether by speech or action.

Fa-huwa khayrun lahu 'inda rabbihi (it is better for him with his Lord): i.e., it is better for him in the Hereafter for the one who venerates the sacred things of Allah and does not violate them.

Illa ma yutla 'alaykum (except what is recited to you): i.e., its prohibition, namely carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah.

Fa-ijtanibu al-rijs (so avoid the abomination): i.e., avoid the worship of idols.

Wa-ijtanibu qawl al-zur (and avoid the word of falsehood): it is lying, and the greatest lying is that which is about Allah, the Most High, as well as shirk and false testimony.

Hunafa' lillah (upright to Allah): monotheists devoted to Him, turning away from every religion to Islam.

Kharra min al-sama' (he falls from the sky): i.e., he falls.

Fa-takhtafahu al-tayr (so the birds snatch him): i.e., they seize him swiftly.

Sha'a'ir Allah (the symbols of Allah): the markers of His religion, and here they are the camels (budn), by choosing the good, fat ones among them.

Fa-innaha min taqwa al-qulub (for it is from the piety of hearts): i.e., their veneration arises from the piety of their hearts.

Lakum fiha manafi' (for you in them are benefits): among them, riding them and carrying upon them what does not harm them, and drinking their milk.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 34–37:

Explanation of the words:

*Mansakan* (a rite, sacrifice): That is, sacrificial animals from the beast of cattle (al-an'am) by which they draw near to Allah the Exalted. The place of slaughter is also called a *mansak*.

*Fa-lahu aslimu* (so to Him submit): That is, submit outwardly and inwardly to His command and prohibition.

*Wa bashshir al-mukhbitin* (and give good tidings to the humble): That is, the obedient, the humble, the submissive.

*Wajilat qulubuhum* (whose hearts tremble): That is, they fear Allah the Exalted lest they have fallen short in obeying Him.

*Al-budn* (the camels for sacrifice): plural of *badanah*, which is what is driven to the Sacred Precinct of camels and cattle to be slaughtered, drawing near to Allah the Exalted.

*Min sha'a'ir Allah* (among the rites of Allah): That is, among the marks of His religion and the manifestations of His worship.

*Sawaff* (standing in line): plural of *saffah*, which is the one standing on three legs with its left forelimb tied.

*Fa-idha wajabat junubuha* (then when their sides fall): That is, after they fall on their sides upon the ground, with no life in them.

*Al-qani' wal-mu'tarr* (the contented and the one who approaches without asking): *Al-qani'* is the one who asks, and *al-mu'tarr* is the one who presents himself to a man without asking, out of modesty and chastity.

*Kadhalika sakhkharnaha* (thus We subjected them): That is, in this same manner of subjection We subjected them to you, so that you may ride them, carry on them, and milk them.

*La'allakum tashkurun* (that you may be grateful): That is, so that you may thank Allah the Exalted by praising Him and obeying Him.

*Lan yanal Allaha luhumuha* (it is not their meat that reaches Allah): That is, no meat or blood is raised up to Allah, but piety reaches Him through doing what He has commanded and abstaining from what He has forbidden.

*Li-tukabbiru Allaha 'ala ma hadakum* (that you may magnify Allah for having guided you): That is, you say "Allahu akbar" after the five prayers during the days of tashriq, thanking Him for His guidance to you.

*Wa bashshir al-muhsinin* (and give good tidings to the good-doers): That is, those who intend by worship the face of Allah alone and perform it in the lawful manner.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues in directing and guiding the believers to what perfects them and makes them happy in both abodes. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And for every nation We have appointed a rite (mansak)﴾, that is, for every nation of the earlier peoples, from among the people of faith and submission, We appointed a place of rite where they worship Us, and a *mansak*, that is, a sacrifice of offering, by which they draw near to Us. And His saying: ﴿that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of the beast of cattle﴾, that is, We legislated for them the worship of sacrificing offerings for a wisdom: that they should mention Our name over the slaughter of what they slaughter and the sacrifice of what they sacrifice, by saying "In the name of Allah, Allah is greatest." And His saying the Exalted: ﴿So your God is one God﴾, that is, so your object of worship, O people, is one object of worship, ﴿so to Him submit﴾ with your faces, and single Him out with your worship. Then He said to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And give good tidings to the humble﴾ of Our good pleasure and entry into the abode of Our honour. He described the humble, identifying them as those who receive the good tidings upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah, saying: ﴿who, when Allah is mentioned﴾ before them or among them ﴿their hearts tremble﴾, that is, they fear, feeling their shortcoming in obeying Him, failing to render Him thanks, and being heedless of remembering Him, ﴿and the steadfast over what has afflicted them﴾ of trials, so they do not grow impatient or resentful, but say: "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return." ﴿And those who establish the prayer﴾, that is, by performing it at its times, in the houses of Allah with His worshippers who are believers, with its conditions, pillars and sunnas complete, ﴿and from what We have provided them they spend﴾, whether little or much, spending in pursuit of the pleasure of their Lord, thanking Allah for what He has given them and submitting to what He has legislated and made obligatory upon them.

And His saying the Exalted: ﴿And the camels We have made for you among the rites of Allah﴾, that is, the camels and cattle that are sent as offerings to the Sacred Precinct, We have made these among the rites of our religion and the manifestations of our worship. ﴿In them is good for you﴾, a great good and a great reward with your Lord on the day you meet Him, for no one draws near on the day of the Festival of Sacrifice with anything better than blood shed in the way of Allah. ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them﴾, that is, say "In the name of Allah, Allah is greatest" at their slaughter. And His saying: ﴿standing in line﴾, that is, standing on three legs with the left forelimb tied. When you slaughter them and they fall, that is, drop on their sides upon the earth dead, ﴿then eat from them and feed the contented one who asks you and the one who approaches you without asking out of modesty﴾. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿Thus We have subjected them to you﴾, that is, in the same manner that We subjected them to you, so that you may ride, milk, slaughter and eat them; We subjected them to you so that you may thank Us through obedience and remembrance.

And His saying the Exalted in the last verse of this context, which is [37]: ﴿It is not their meat that reaches Allah, nor their blood﴾, that is, no meat or blood is raised up to Him, and the good pleasure from Him is not attained by it; rather, piety—through sincerity, performing what is obligatory and recommended, and abstaining from what is forbidden and disliked—this is what is raised up to Him and attains the level of His good pleasure.

And His saying: ﴿Thus He has subjected them to you﴾, that is, in the same manner, the subjection by which He subjected them to you, for the purpose that you magnify Allah for having guided you to faith and submission; so magnify Allah at the slaughter of the camels and the sacrifice of offerings, at the performance of the rites, and after the five prayers during the days of tashriq. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿And give good tidings to the good-doers﴾: Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger and the one who conveys from Him, Muhammad ﷺ, to give good tidings by his name to the good-doers who perfected faith and submission, who made Allah one and worshipped Him by what He legislated and in the manner He legislated, following in that the guidance of His Messenger and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The sacrifice of offerings is legislated in all the divine religions, and it is evidence that there is no god but Allah, since the unity of the legislation indicates the unity of the Legislator.

The secret of the legislation of sacrificial offering is that Allah the Exalted be mentioned; therefore it is obligatory to mention the name of Allah over the slaughter of what is slaughtered and the sacrifice of what is sacrificed, with the words "In the name of Allah, Allah is greatest."

2- Definition of the humble (mukhbitin): those who receive the glad tidings of Allah's good pleasure and His noble neighbourhood.

3- The obligation to mention the name of Allah over the beast of cattle.

4- Explanation of the manner of sacrificing the camels, and the prohibition of taking from them before their death and the departure of their soul.

5- Recommendation to eat from the offerings and the obligation to feed the poor and the needy from them.

6- The obligation to thank Allah for every blessing.

7- The legislation of takbir during the performance of rites, such as stoning the pillars and slaughtering what is slaughtered, and after the five prayers during the days of tashriq.

8- The virtue of excellence (ihsan), and the success of the good-doers with glad tidings upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

*Wa bashshir al-mukhbitin* (and give good tidings to the humble): That is, the obedient, the humble, the submissive.

*Wajilat qulubuhum* (whose hearts tremble): That is, they fear Allah the Exalted lest they have fallen short in obeying Him.

*Al-budn* (the camels for sacrifice): plural of *badanah*, which is what is driven to the Sacred Precinct of camels and cattle to be slaughtered, drawing near to Allah the Exalted.

*Min sha'a'ir Allah* (among the rites of Allah): That is, among the marks of His religion and the manifestations of His worship.

*Sawaff* (standing in line): plural of *saffah*, which is the one standing on three legs with its left forelimb tied.

*Fa-idha wajabat junubuha* (then when their sides fall): That is, after they fall on their sides upon the ground, with no life in them.
