Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 38–41:

Explanation of the words:

Yudafi' (يدافع): one reading has yadfa'u, meaning He repels the treachery (ghawa'il) of the polytheists and what they plot against the believers.

Khawwan (خوان): one who is much given to betrayal of his trust and his covenants.

Kafur (كفور): one who denies his Lord, His Book, His Messenger and His blessings upon him.

Bi-annahum zulimu (بأنهم ظلموا): that is, because of the wrong the polytheists did to them.

Bi-ghayri haqq (بغير حق): that is, something that would justify their expulsion from their homes.

Illa an yaqulu Rabbuna Allah (إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله): that is, except for their saying, "Our Lord is Allah," and Allah is the Truth. Yet does saying the truth justify the expulsion of the one who says it?

Sawami' wa-biya' (صوامع وبيع): the places of worship of monks and the churches of the Christians.

Wa-salawat (وصلوات): the places of worship of the Jews; in Hebrew its singular is ṣalūthā.

Wa-masajid (ومساجد): that is, the houses of prayer of the Muslims.

Man yansuruhu (من ينصره): that is, who supports His religion and His believing servants.

Qawiyyun 'Aziz (قوي عزيز): Able to do whatever He wills, Mighty, not prevented from what He wills.

In makkannahum fi'l-ard (إن مكناهم في الأرض): that is, We granted them victory over their enemy and established them in the lands by placing authority in their hands.

Wa-lillahi 'aqibat al-umur (ولله عاقبة الأمور): that is, the final outcome of all creatures' affairs returns to Allah the Exalted, who rewards and punishes.

The meanings of the verses:

The context continues in guiding, instructing and directing the believers. Allah's saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed﴾, means He repels from them the treachery of the polytheists and protects them from their plots and schemes. His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love every treacherous ungrateful one﴾, is a justification: the polytheists who barred the Messenger of Allah and the believers from the Sacred Mosque are the ones who betray their trusts and covenants and disbelieve in their Lord, His Messenger, His Book and what he brought. Since He does not love them, He is against them and not on their side. In contrast, He loves every believer who is sincere in his faith, faithful to his trusts and covenants, and obedient to his Lord; whoever He loves, He defends and protects from his enemies.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against﴾, is in the passive form, and in another reading in the active form (those who fight), and both are readings: that is, those who were fought against by these polytheists have been permitted by Allah the Exalted to fight their polytheist enemies, after they had been prohibited from doing so, for a wisdom known to their Lord. This is the first verse in the Qur'an to bear the character of war, by permitting the believers to engage in it. His saying, ﴿And indeed, Allah is capable of giving them victory﴾, reassures them that He is with them through His support and aid, and He is capable of that. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿who have been evicted from their homes without right﴾, means without any justification for their expulsion, except that they say, "Our Lord is Allah." This is true, and it is no justification for expelling them from their homes and driving them out of their dwellings and lands. This sentence clarifies the basis of the permission given to them to fight and of Allah's support for them. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And were it not for Allah's repelling people by means of others﴾, means that by the people of truth Allah repels the people of falsehood; were it not for this, the people of falsehood would prevail, ﴿and monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques, in which the name of Allah is much mentioned, would have been demolished﴾. This is also a justification and an explanation of the wisdom behind the command to fight: that is, were it not that Allah repels the people of disbelief by means of the people of faith, the people of disbelief would prevail, demolish the places of worship and not permit the believers to worship Allah. The explanation of the words above clarifies the places of worship mentioned, so refer to it.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful, Mighty﴾: that is, Capable, ﴿Mighty﴾, Overpowering. Whoever seeks to support Him, He will support, even if all the people of the earth's regions gather against him. The one whom Allah wishes to support is the one who fights for the sake of Allah so that He is worshipped on earth and nothing is worshipped alongside Him; that is the way of supporting Allah, so let this be known. His saying, ﴿Those who, if We establish them in the land﴾: that is, We make way for them in the land and grant them dominion after subduing their polytheist enemies, so that they rule and lead, establish prayer in the manner required of them, give the zakat due on their wealth, enjoin what is good, that is, Islam and entering into it and upholding it, and forbid what is evil, that is, polytheism, disbelief and disobedience to Allah and His Messenger. These are the ones most deserving of Allah's support, because they fight to support Allah, Mighty and Majestic. His saying, ﴿And to Allah belongs the outcome of all affairs﴾, informs that the final return of every matter is to Him, the Exalted, who judges it by what is true and just, rewarding righteous deeds and punishing corrupt ones, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. Accordingly, let one be mindful of Allah, be God-conscious in secret and in public, rely upon Him, and turn to Him in repentance, for the return of every matter is to Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Allah's true promise to defend the believers who are sincere in their faith.

2- Allah's abhorrence of the people of disbelief and treachery.

3- The legitimacy of fighting to raise the word of Allah, so that He alone is worshipped and His friends are not persecuted.

4- Explanation of the secret of the permission to wage jihad and of Allah's support for His friends who fight for His sake.

5- Explanation of the foundations of the state whose people Allah makes heirs to the land and establishes therein, namely:

Establishing prayer – giving zakat – enjoining good – forbidding evil.

Khawwan (خوان): one who is much given to betrayal of his trust and his covenants.

Kafur (كفور): one who denies his Lord, His Book, His Messenger and His blessings upon him.

Bi-annahum zulimu (بأنهم ظلموا): that is, because of the wrong the polytheists did to them.

Bi-ghayri haqq (بغير حق): that is, something that would justify their expulsion from their homes.

Illa an yaqulu Rabbuna Allah (إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله): that is, except for their saying, "Our Lord is Allah," and Allah is the Truth. Yet does saying the truth justify the expulsion of the one who says it?

Sawami' wa-biya' (صوامع وبيع): the places of worship of monks and the churches of the Christians.

Wa-salawat (وصلوات): the places of worship of the Jews; in Hebrew its singular is ṣalūthā.

Wa-masajid (ومساجد): that is, the houses of prayer of the Muslims.

Man yansuruhu (من ينصره): that is, who supports His religion and His believing servants.

Qawiyyun 'Aziz (قوي عزيز): Able to do whatever He wills, Mighty, not prevented from what He wills.

In contrast, He loves every believer who is sincere in his faith, faithful to his trusts and covenants, and obedient to his Lord; whoever He loves, He defends and protects from his enemies.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 42–46:

Explanation of the words:

"And if they deny you": That is, if your people deny you, then (the peoples) before them denied (their prophets): the people of Noah, so do not grieve, for you are not alone in being denied.

"And the companions of Madyan": They are the people of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him.

"And Musa was denied": That is, Pharaoh and his household, the Copts, denied him.

"Then I gave the disbelievers respite": That is, I gave them time and did not hasten the punishment upon them.

"Then I seized them": That is, with a punishment that uprooted them.

"Then how was My rejection": That is, how was My denunciation of them for their denial and disbelief? Was it fitting its due place? Yes, for the interrogative is for affirmation.

"It is fallen upon its roofs": That is, collapsed upon its ceilings.

"A deserted well": That is, abandoned, no water is drawn from it because its people have died.

"And a lofty palace": Raised high and plastered with gypsum (jass).

"For indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded": That is, indeed the matter (the story) does not blind the eyes; the defect is not in their eyes but in their hearts, where desire has blinded them, lust has corrupted them, and blind imitation of people of ignorance and misguidance has done so.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in calling Quraysh to faith and monotheism. Though guidance for the believers is interspersed, when He permitted the believers to fight the polytheists, He explained the requirements of this permission, guaranteed them victory, and informed them that the outcome of affairs belongs to Him alone, and that He will judge with truth and justice among His servants on the day they meet Him. He said to His Messenger ﷺ, consoling him regarding the polytheists' denial of him: ﴿And if they deny you﴾, O Messenger, regarding what you brought of monotheism, prophethood, resurrection and recompense on the Day of Judgment, then do not despair and do not grieve. ﴿Indeed, before them denied﴾, that is, before your deniers from Quraysh, the Arabs and the Jews, ﴿the people of Noah and ʿĀd﴾, the people of Hud, ﴿and Thamūd﴾, the people of Salih, ﴿and the people of Abraham, the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan, and Musa was denied﴾ also, despite what We had brought them of clear signs. My practice with them was that I gave them respite, that is, I extended their time and let out their rope, until, when they reached the extreme of disbelief, obstinacy, wrongdoing and tyranny, and the word of punishment was due against them, I seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the All-Powerful. ﴿So how was My rejection?﴾ — that is, My denunciation of them? Your Lord's denunciation was fitting its due place, and those mentioned were not the only ones seized... ﴿How many a city﴾ great, prosperous with its men, wealth and authority ﴿We destroyed while it was wrongdoing﴾, that is, persisting in wrongdoing, namely polytheism and denial. ﴿So it is fallen upon its roofs﴾, that is, collapsed upon its ceilings. And how many a well of sweet water that was a source of drink for them is now abandoned, and how many a lofty palace, raised high and plastered with gypsum, after its people died and left it. This is what the four verses [42, 43, 44, 45] contained. As for the last verse of this passage, the Truthful, Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Have they not traveled through the land so that they would have hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear?﴾ urging the deniers among the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Arabs to travel through the lands to observe the traces of those who were destroyed, perhaps that will gain them a new life in their thinking and outlook, so that they have living, aware hearts by which they understand Our address to them, as We call them to their salvation and happiness, or ears by which they hear the call of counsel and goodness that We direct to them through Our Book and Our Messenger. Eyes that see without aware hearts and attentive ears are of no benefit. ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blinded.﴾

This is the essence of the matter: Yes, let them travel, perhaps they will gain lessons and admonitions that revive their hearts and all their dull senses.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The denial of messengers and of those who call to truth and good is a constant practice among humankind, with its causes, the most prominent of which are blind imitation, preserving material interests, and darkness of the heart arising from shirk and sins.

He said to His Messenger ﷺ, consoling him regarding the polytheists' denial of him: ﴿And if they deny you﴾, O Messenger, regarding what you brought of monotheism, prophethood, resurrection and recompense on the Day of Judgment, then do not despair and do not grieve. ﴿Indeed, before them denied﴾, that is, before your deniers from Quraysh, the Arabs and the Jews, ﴿the people of Noah and ʿĀd﴾, the people of Hud, ﴿and Thamūd﴾, the people of Salih, ﴿and the people of Abraham, the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan, and Musa was denied﴾ also, despite what We had brought them of clear signs. My practice with them was that I gave them respite, that is, I extended their time and let out their rope, until, when they reached the extreme of disbelief, obstinacy, wrongdoing and tyranny, and the word of punishment was due against them, I seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the All-Powerful. ﴿So how was My rejection?﴾ — that is, My denunciation of them? Your Lord's denunciation was fitting its due place, and those mentioned were not the only ones seized... ﴿How many a city﴾ great, prosperous with its men, wealth and authority ﴿We destroyed while it was wrongdoing﴾, that is, persisting in wrongdoing, namely polytheism and denial. ﴿So it is fallen upon its roofs﴾, that is, collapsed upon its ceilings. And how many a well of sweet water that was a source of drink for them is now abandoned, and how many a lofty palace, raised high and plastered with gypsum, after its people died and left it. This is what the four verses [42, 43, 44, 45] contained. As for the last verse of this passage, the Truthful, Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Have they not traveled through the land so that they would have hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear?﴾ urging the deniers among the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Arabs to travel through the lands to observe the traces of those who were destroyed, perhaps that will gain them a new life in their thinking and outlook, so that they have living, aware hearts by which they understand Our address to them, as We call them to their salvation and happiness, or ears by which they hear the call of counsel and goodness that We direct to them through Our Book and Our Messenger. Eyes that see without aware hearts and attentive ears are of no benefit. ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but it is the hearts within the breasts that are blinded.﴾

This is the essence of the matter: Yes, let them travel, perhaps they will gain lessons and admonitions that revive their hearts and all their dull senses.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The denial of messengers and of those who call to truth and good is a constant practice among humankind, with its causes, the most prominent of which are blind imitation, preserving material interests, and darkness of the heart arising from shirk and sins.

2- Aspects of God's power in destroying nations and peoples who wrong, after giving them respite and warning.

3- The legitimacy of seeking lessons and drawing them from the traces of those who were destroyed.

4- What matters is inner insight of the heart, not sight: how many a blind person sees the realities and paths of salvation better than one with sharp, keen eyesight. Hence it is incumbent upon the servant to guard his insight more than his eyes, by avoiding what destroys the hearts: lying, falsehoods, superstitions, pride, vanity, and love and hatred for other than God's sake.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 47–51:

Explanation of the words:

Yasta'jilunaka bil-'adhab (they ask you to hasten the punishment): i.e., they demand, urging you on, the punishment about which you warned them from Allah.

Ka-alfi sanatin mimma ta'uddun (like a thousand years of what you count): i.e., of the days of this world, each of twenty-four hours.

Wa ka'ayyin min qaryatin (and how many a town): i.e., many towns, namely the capitals and metropolises that gathered every aspect of civilization.

Amlaytu laha (I gave it respite): i.e., I granted it time, so the days of its life were prolonged, and I did not hasten its punishment.

Nadhirun mubin (a clear warner): one who warns, i.e., who clearly warns of the consequence of disbelief and wrongdoing.

Lahum maghfiratun wa rizqun karim (for them is forgiveness and a generous provision): i.e., a covering over their sins and good provision in Paradise.

Sa'aw fi ayatina mu'ajizin (they strove against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them): i.e., they worked with diligence and effort to turn people away from faith in Our signs and from what they carry of a call to monotheism and to abandoning polytheism and sins.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble discourse continues to guide and direct the Messenger ﷺ in his call, to patience and endurance, saying to him: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment﴾, i.e., the polytheists among your people ask you to hasten the punishment with which you threatened and warned them, ﴿and Allah will not fail His promise﴾, for He has promised it and it will surely befall them; and this was fulfilled at Badr. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾. Therefore, He, exalted is He, does not hasten, while they hasten. The day of Allah is a thousand years, while their days are twenty-four hours. So when He sets a day for their punishment, it means the punishment will not descend upon them until a thousand years have passed; half a day is five hundred years, a quarter of a day is two hundred and fifty years, and so on. Thus man hastens and grows impatient, while Allah, mighty and majestic, fulfills His promise at the time He has set, and the urgency of the criminals does not hurry Him toward the punishment. This meaning is confirmed by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had it not been for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them﴾ [Verse 53] of Surah al-'Ankabut. This is what the first verse [47] indicates.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a town﴾, i.e., a great city, ﴿I gave respite to﴾, i.e., I granted it time and extended the days of its existence, while it was wrongdoing through polytheism and sins; then after that respite and delay I seized it. ﴿And to Me is the final return﴾, i.e., the destiny of everything and its return is to Me; there is no god but Me and no lord besides Me. So there is no sense in these polytheists hastening the punishment, for whether they are punished in this world or not, their destiny is with Allah, exalted is He, and He will recompense them for what they earned with a just recompense in the abode of misery and everlasting punishment. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you﴾. So I am not a god, nor a lord, in whose hand is your punishment if you disobey me or your blessing if you obey me; I am only a servant commanded to warn the disobedient of the Lord of His punishment and to give good news to the people of His obedience of His mercy. This is the meaning of verse [50]. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, and this necessarily implies that they abandoned polytheism and sins, they have forgiveness for their sins and generous provision with their Lord, which is Paradise, the abode of bliss. ﴿And those who strove against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them﴾, i.e., they worked earnestly and eagerly to turn people away from the signs of Allah so that they would not believe in them or act upon the guidance and light within them, seeking to frustrate Allah, thinking they could overcome Him, while Allah prevails over His affair, supports His religion and His friends. Those are the farthest in evil and polytheism, the companions of the blazing fire, abiding in it forever and ever.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Haste is part of human nature, but hastening Allah and His Messenger toward punishment is folly, recklessness, misguidance and disbelief.

2- What is with Allah in the higher realm differs entirely from what is in this lower realm.

3- The consequence of wrongdoing is dire, and in the report: "Wrongdoing leaves homes as desolate wastelands," i.e., ruined and empty.

4- Clarification of the mission of the messengers, which is only conveyance together with warning and giving good news.

5- Clarification of the destiny of believers and disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verse 52–57:

Explanation of the words:

﻿"Min rasulin wa la nabiyyin" (no messenger or prophet): The rasul (messenger) is a male from among the children of Adam to whom a law (shar') is revealed and who is commanded to convey it; the nabi (prophet) confirms the law of the one before him.

"Tamanna fi umniyyatihi" (when he recited, in his recitation): i.e., he recited, in his recitation.

"Thumma yuhkimu Allahu ayatihi" (then Allah makes His verses firm): i.e., after the removal of what Satan cast into the recitation, Allah establishes His verses, that is, confirms them.

"Fitnatan lilladhina fi qulubihim maradun" (a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease): i.e., a test for those in whose hearts is the disease of polytheism and doubt.

"Wal-qasiyati qulubuhum" (and those whose hearts are hardened): they are the polytheists.

"Fatakhbata lahu qulubuhum" (and their hearts may humble themselves to it): i.e., their hearts become submissive and humbly fearful before it.

"Fi miryatin minhu" (in doubt concerning it): i.e., in doubt and suspicion regarding the Qur'an.

"Adhabu yawmin 'aqim" (the punishment of a barren day): it is the punishment of the Day of Badr, when it was a barren day with no good in it.

"Fi jannati an-na'im" (in gardens of bliss): i.e., gardens full of bliss whose description cannot reach its extent.

"Fa-lahum 'adhabun muhin" (then for them is a humiliating punishment): i.e., its companion is humiliated in it, so it is a punishment of body and soul.

Meaning of the verses:

After the first consolation given to the Prophet ﷺ, contained in Allah's words: ﴿And if they deny you, then the people of Noah denied before them...﴾ [al-Hajj: 42] etc., Allah mentions a second consolation: that the Prophet ﷺ was reciting in his prayer around the Ka'bah, Surah an-Najm, while the polytheists around the Ka'bah were listening. "Fatakhbata lahu qulubuhum" (and their hearts may humble themselves to it): i.e., their hearts become submissive and humbly fearful before it.

"Fi miryatin minhu" (in doubt concerning it): i.e., in doubt and suspicion regarding the Qur'an.

"Adhabu yawmin 'aqim" (the punishment of a barren day): it is the punishment of the Day of Badr, when it was a barren day with no good in it.

"Fi jannati an-na'im" (in gardens of bliss): i.e., gardens full of bliss whose description cannot reach its extent.

"Fa-lahum 'adhabun muhin" (then for them is a humiliating punishment): i.e., its companion is humiliated in it, so it is a punishment of body and soul.

Meaning of the verses:

After the first consolation given to the Prophet ﷺ, contained in Allah's words: ﴿And if they deny you, then the people of Noah denied before them...﴾ [al-Hajj: 42] etc., Allah mentions a second consolation: that the Prophet ﷺ was reciting in his prayer around the Ka'bah, Surah an-Najm, while the polytheists around the Ka'bah were listening. When he reached Allah's words: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ [an-Najm: 19-20], Satan cast into the ears of the polytheists the following words: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for." The polytheists rejoiced at what they heard, thinking that the Prophet ﷺ had recited it and that Allah had revealed it. When he prostrated at the end of the surah, they prostrated with him, except for an old man who could not prostrate, so he took a handful of dust and prostrated upon it. It spread that Muhammad had reconciled with his people, until the emigrants returned from Abyssinia. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was distressed and grieved over this, so Allah revealed this verse as consolation to him, saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger﴾ bearing a message he conveys, ﴿nor a prophet﴾ confirming the message of a prophet before him, ﴿except that when he recited﴾ i.e., recited, ﴿Satan threw [something] into his recitation﴾ i.e., into his recitation, ﴿but Allah abolishes what Satan throws in﴾ i.e., removes and nullifies it, ﴿[words] from the hearts of the disbelievers, His allies﴾, ﴿then Allah makes His verses precise﴾ after the removal of what Satan said, so He confirms them, and no addition or subtraction is accepted. And Allah is Knowing of His creation, their conditions and their deeds; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He is Wise in His management and His law. This is His practice with His messengers and prophets, so do not despair, O Messenger of Allah, and do not grieve. Then Allah explains the wisdom in this practice, saying: ﴿That He may make what Satan throws in a trial﴾ i.e., of words in the recitation of the Prophet or messenger, ﴿for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿and the hardened of heart﴾ who are the polytheists. The meaning of "fitnah" here is an ordeal by which they increase in misguidance upon their misguidance and distance from the truth beyond their existing distance, for Satan casts into the hearts of his allies only for a trial, i.e., an increase in disbelief and error.

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension﴾ are a report from Him about the state of the polytheists: that they are in opposition to Allah and His Messenger, far off in what they believe, what they do, what they say, and what they imagine, in complete contradiction to what Allah commands and calls them to in belief, speech, action, conception and perception. Allah's words: ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and believe in it, and their hearts humble themselves to it﴾ this is part of the reason contained in Allah's practice of casting Satan's words into the recitation of the messenger or prophet. The first part was contained in His words: ﴿That He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and the hardened of heart﴾; this is the second part, i.e., ﴿and that those who have been given knowledge﴾ of Allah, His verses and His management, ﴿that it is the truth from your Lord﴾ i.e., that casting, abrogation and the subsequent confirmation of the verses, ﴿and believe in it, and their hearts humble themselves to it﴾ i.e., become tranquil and calm and submissive before it, so that they increase in guidance. Allah's words: ﴿And indeed, Allah guides those who believe to a straight path﴾ are a report from Him about His action toward His allies, the believers who are mindful of Him: that He guides them throughout their lives and in all their conditions to a straight path that leads them to His pleasure and Paradise, by protecting them from Satan, granting them success, and helping them to obey the Most Merciful, glorified and exalted is He. Allah's words: ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾ i.e., about the Qur'an: whether it is the speech of Allah, whether it is the truth, whether following it is beneficial. This doubt will continue for those hard-hearted people, the people of extreme dissension, ﴿until the Hour comes upon them suddenly﴾ i.e., unexpectedly, and it is the Resurrection, ﴿or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day﴾ i.e., with no good for them in it, and it is the Day of Badr; that was accomplished for them, and at that point their doubt ended and they knew that it is the truth, when knowledge no longer benefits.

He is the just, true Judge who judges among His servants by what was mentioned in the verse: those who believed in Him, His Messenger, and what he brought, and did righteous deeds, both obligatory and voluntary, after abandoning polytheism and sins, He will admit to Gardens of Bliss; and those who disbelieved in Him, His Messenger, and what he brought, and denied Allah's verses containing His laws and the explanation of His obedience, did not believe and did not do righteous deeds, but did the opposite, which is evil deeds: those are the far-off ones in lowliness and baseness, for them is a humiliating punishment that breaks their noses in abasement and debasement of themselves.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of Allah's practice regarding Satan's casting into the recitation of a messenger or prophet as a trial.

2- Explanation that in this trial those with diseased and hardened hearts perish, while believers emerge with greater certainty and greater guidance.

3- Explanation of Allah's judgment among His servants on the Day of Resurrection, honoring the people of faith and piety and humiliating the people of polytheism and sin.

4- Manifestation of the fulfillment of what Allah reported about the criminals of Quraysh, for they persisted in their doubt until they perished at Badr.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 58–62:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Those who emigrated⦆ (wa-alladhina hajaru): that is, they left the abodes of disbelief and went to the abode of faith, the illuminated city of Madinah.

"In the way of Allah" (fi sabil Allah): that is, they left their homes not for worldly gain, but to worship Allah, to support His religion and His allies.

"He will surely provide for them a goodly provision" (layarzuqannahum rizqan hasanan): that is, in Paradise, where their souls are in the crops of green birds that graze in Paradise.

"He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with" (layudkhilannahum madkhalan yarduna): that is, Paradise, on the Day of Resurrection.

"That" (dhalika): that is, the matter just mentioned, so remember it and do not forget it.

"Then he is wronged" (thumma baghā ʿalayhi): that is, he is wronged after he has punished his enemy with the same wrong that was done to him.

"He causes the night to enter into the day" (yulij al-layl fi al-nahar): that is, He makes part of the night enter the day and the reverse, according to the seasons of the year, just as He daily makes the night enter the day when the day comes, and makes the day enter the night when the night comes.

"That Allah is the Truth" (bi-anna Allah huwa al-haqq): that is, the true God whose worship is obligatory to the exclusion of all others.

"And that what they call upon besides Him" (min dunihi): that is, idols, images and other things, is falsehood itself.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to explain the judgment of Allah Most High among His servants. He mentioned what He decreed for the people of faith and righteous deeds and what He decreed for the people of disbelief and denial, and here He mentions what He decreed for the people of emigration and jihad. So the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And those who emigrated in the way of Allah⦆, that is, they left their homes for the sake of obeying Allah and supporting His religion, ﴿then were killed⦆ at the hands of Allah's enemies, the polytheists, ﴿or died⦆ naturally, without being killed. ﴿Allah will surely provide for them a goodly provision⦆ in Paradise, where their souls are in the crops of green birds that graze in Paradise and take shelter in lamps suspended beneath the Throne. ﴿He will surely admit them⦆ on the Day of Resurrection ﴿to an entrance that they will be pleased with⦆, which is Paradise. As for His saying, Most High: ﴿And indeed, Allah is surely the best of providers⦆, that is, He is the best of those who provide: what He provides them is the best, purest and most abundant provision. And His saying: ﴿And indeed, Allah is surely All-Knowing, Most Forbearing⦆: All-Knowing of His servants and of their deeds, apparent and hidden; Most Forbearing, who pardons and overlooks some of the lapses of His believing servants, forgiving them and concealing them from others, since no servant is free from sin except those whom Allah has protected, namely His prophets and messengers.

And His saying, Most High: ﴿That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was made to suffer⦆, that is, the matter is as I have explained to you, ﴿and whoever retaliates with the like of what he was made to suffer⦆, that is, whoever takes from his oppressor an amount equal to what was taken from him, as retribution. ﴿Then he is wronged⦆ afterward by the one who wronged him, for the oppressed, at first and at last, is guaranteed support by Allah Most High. His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is surely Pardoning, Forgiving⦆ contains an indication encouraging the believer to pardon his brother when he wrongs him, for pardon is better than retaliation. This is like His saying, Most High: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it; but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah. Indeed, He does not like wrongdoers. And whoever avenges himself after being wronged – those, there is no path [of blame] against them﴾ [al-Shura: 40–41]. And His saying: ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing⦆ means: the One who is able to make the night enter the day and the day enter the night, such that when one of them comes the other departs, and when one of them shortens the other lengthens, is All-Hearing of His servants' statements and All-Seeing of their deeds and conditions, and is able to grant victory to those among His allies who are wronged. His saying, Most High: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth⦆, that is, the true God who deserves to be worshipped, and that what they call upon besides Him of idols and images is falsehood. That is, the aforementioned matter of Allah's power, His knowledge and His support of His allies is so because Allah is the true God, and what they worship besides Him of deities is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High over His creation, the Subduer of them, the Majestic over them, the Great, the Mighty, than whom nothing is greater.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the virtue of emigration in the way of Allah, to the extent that it equals jihad in the way of Allah.

2- Permissibility of retaliation on condition of equivalence, and pardon is better than retaliation.

3- Explanation of the manifestations of lordship, namely knowledge and power, which necessitate worshipping Allah alone and the invalidity of worshipping others.

4- Affirmation of the attributes of Allah Most High: knowledge, forbearance, forgiveness, hearing, seeing, pardon, exaltation over creation, and the greatness that necessitates worshipping Him and abandoning the worship of anyone else.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 63–66:

Explanation of the words:

"Alam tara" (Have you not seen?): i.e., have you not known.

"Mukhdarrah" (green): i.e., covered with grass, herbage and plants.

"Al-Ghaniyy al-Hamid" (the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy): the One who is independent of everything other than Himself, and praised in His earth and His heavens.

"Sakhkhara lakum ma fi al-ard" (He has subjected to you what is in the earth): i.e., He made it easy for you to possess it, to dispose of it, and to benefit from it.

"Ahyakum" (He gave you life): i.e., He brought you into existence as living beings after you were non-existent.

"La-kafur" (indeed ungrateful): i.e., greatly given to disbelief and denial of his Lord and of His blessings upon him.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish Tawhid (the Oneness of God) by mentioning the manifestations of His power, knowledge and wisdom. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Have you not seen﴾, O Messenger, ﴿that Allah sends down water from the sky﴾, i.e., rain, so that the earth becomes after the descent of the rain upon it ﴿green﴾ with grass, plants and crops. And His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is Subtle﴾ toward His servants, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with what sets them right, harms them and benefits them.

And His saying: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth﴾, i.e., by creation, ownership and disposal, ﴿and indeed Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ — independent of His creation, ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., praised in the earth and the heavens for His beautiful creation and great bounty. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you what is in the earth﴾, of animals and beasts of their varied kinds, ﴿and the ship﴾, i.e., He subjected to you the ship, meaning the boats, ﴿running upon the sea by His command﴾, i.e., by His permission and subjugation. ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth﴾, i.e., lest it fall upon the earth, ﴿except by His permission﴾, i.e., it does not fall except when He permits it to do so. And His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is, toward the people, Kind and Merciful﴾ — from the manifestations of His kindness and mercy toward them is that mercy which is evident in every aspect of their lives: in carrying them, in their nursing, in their nourishment, in their sleep, in their wakefulness, in obtaining their provision, in His pardon of their slips, in not hastening punishment upon them after they have deserved it, in sending the messengers and in sending down the scriptures. So glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who gave you life﴾ by bringing you into being and creating you from nothing, ﴿then He causes you to die﴾ at the end of your terms, ﴿then He gives you life again﴾ and resurrects you to recompense you for your deeds. Despite all these blessings, man disbelieves in them: he leaves the remembrance of his Lord and His thanks, mentions others and gives thanks to other than Him. These manifestations of the power, knowledge and wisdom of the Lord, and those blessings and favors, both apparent and hidden, necessitate faith in Allah, make His worship, Oneness, remembrance and thanks obligatory, and make the worship of other than Him foolishness and intellectual error whose extent cannot be measured and whose limit cannot be known.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Establishing Tawhid by mentioning its requirements of power and grace.

2- Affirming the attributes of Allah: the Subtle, the All-Aware, the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy, the Kind, the Merciful, the Giver of life, the Causer of death.

3- Explaining Allah's bounty and favor upon His creation.

4- The manifestations of Allah's power in holding back the sky from falling upon the earth, and in giving life, causing death and resurrection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verses 67–72:

Explanation of the words:

*Ja'alna mansakan*: that is, a place in which they worship through sacrifices or other acts.

*Fa-la yunazi'unaka*: that is, they should not dispute with you.

*Hudan mustaqim*: that is, a straight religion, which is Islam, the true religion of God.

*Fi kitab*: this is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

*Ma lam yunazzil bihi sultanan*: that is, proof and evidence.

*Al-munkar*: that is, the denial indicated by the frowning and scowling of the face.

*Yastuna*: they attack, they assault.

*Bi-sharrin min dhalikum*: this is the Fire.

And His words: ﴿Say: "Shall I inform you of something worse than that?"﴾, that is, say to them, O Our Messenger: shall I inform you of something worse than what you dislike, namely those who recite God's verses to you? 1. Establishing the reality that every community in which God sent a messenger, He prescribed for it acts of worship by which He is worshipped.

2. Commending the abandonment of disputation over self-evident matters and turning away from them.

3. Affirming God's knowledge of every hidden and manifest thing, small and great, in the heavens and the earth.

4. Affirming the doctrine of divine decree and predestination through the affirmation of the Book that contains it, which is the Preserved Tablet.

5. Showing the intense hatred of the polytheists toward the monotheists when they are called to monotheism and reminded of the signs.

6. The permissibility of angering the wrongdoer with the true word that displeases him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 22, verse 77–78:

Explanation of the words:

"واعبدوا ربكم" (So worship your Lord): i.e., obey Him in His command and His prohibition, with a veneration that is the utmost veneration and a humility before Him that is the utmost humility.

"وافعلوا الخير" (And do good): i.e., of all that Allah has urged you to do and has encouraged you towards, of righteous speech and deeds.

"لعلكم تفلحون" (So that you may be successful): i.e., so that you may win salvation from the Fire and entry into the Garden.

"حق جهاده" (with the striving due to Him): i.e., the true striving that Allah has prescribed and commanded, which is the striving against disbelief, Satan, the self and desire.

"اجتباكم" (He has chosen you): i.e., He has selected you to bear the call of Allah to mankind in its entirety.

"من حرج" (any hardship): i.e., any constraint or obligation that cannot be borne.

"ملة أبيكم" (the religion of your father): i.e., adhere to the religion of your father Ibrahim, which is the worship of Allah alone without partner.

"وفي هذا" (and in this): i.e., the Qur'an.

"اعتصموا بالله" (hold fast to Allah): i.e., hold firmly to His religion and trust in His support and His good reward.

"ونعم النصير" (and excellent is the Helper): i.e., He, exalted is He, is the excellent Helper, the one who gives you support.

Meaning of the verses:

After establishing the creed in its three parts: monotheism, prophethood, and resurrection with recompense, the Lord, blessed and exalted, addressed the Muslims with the title of faith, saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, i.e., you who have believed in Allah as Lord, in Muhammad as Messenger, and in Islam as religion. ﴿Bow and prostrate﴾, He commanded them to establish the prayer. ﴿And worship your Lord﴾, i.e., obey Him in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you, venerating Him with the utmost veneration and humbling yourselves before Him with the utmost humility. ﴿And do good﴾, of all that Allah has urged you to and encouraged you towards of kinds of righteousness and forms of worship. ﴿So that you may be successful﴾, i.e., so that you may qualify thereby for success, which is the winning of Paradise after salvation from the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾: i.e., He also commanded them with a matter of great importance, which is fighting the disbelievers until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah. The meaning of "striving due to Him" is as it should be, exerting all effort and capacity: with the self, with wealth, and with the call. And His saying: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾: this is a favour by which Allah, exalted is He, reminds the believers so that they may thank Allah by doing what He has commanded them. I.e., He did not constrict you in what He has commanded you, but made it expansive: He made repentance available for every sin, made expiation for some sins, granted the traveller and the sick concessions in shortening the prayer and fasting, and for one who does not find water or is unable to use it, tayammum.

And His saying: ﴿The religion of your father Abraham﴾: i.e., adhere to the religion of your father. And His saying: ﴿He named you Muslims﴾: i.e., Allah, majestic is His majesty, is the One who named them Muslims in the earlier scriptures and in the Qur'an, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿He named you Muslims before and in this﴾, i.e., the Qur'an. And His saying: ﴿That the Messenger may be a witness over you and that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾: i.e., He chose you, O believers, for His Islamic religion and named you Muslims, so that the Messenger may be a witness over you on the Day of Resurrection that he has conveyed to you what he was sent with, and you will be witnesses then over all the messengers that they conveyed to their peoples what they were sent with. Accordingly, thank Allah, the Exalted, for this blessing and honour. ﴿So establish the prayer, give the zakah, and hold fast to Allah﴾: i.e., hold firmly to His law in creed, worship, character, conduct, judgement and rule. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He is your Protector﴾: i.e., your Master and the Owner of your affairs. ﴿How excellent a Protector﴾: He, glorified and exalted is He. ﴿And how excellent a Helper﴾: i.e., the Helper for you as long as you are His allies, living in faith and piety.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The virtue of prayer, the nobility of worship, and the doing of good.

2- The legislation of prostration upon recitation of this verse: ﴿And do good, that you may be successful﴾.

3- The merit of striving in the way of Allah, which is fighting the disbelievers, and that the blame of any blamer should not deter the believer in Allah.

4- The virtue of this Muslim community, as it has been given three things that were given to no prophet except one. It was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Go, for there is no hardship upon you," and Allah said to this community: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾. It was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him: "You are a witness over your people," and Allah said: ﴿And that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾. It was said to the Prophet: "Ask and you will be given," and Allah said to this community: ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60]. This is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾.

5- The obligation of prayer and zakah, and adherence to the Shari'ah.

"وفي هذا" (and in this): i.e., the Qur'an.

"اعتصموا بالله" (hold fast to Allah): i.e., hold firmly to His religion and trust in His support and His good reward.

"ونعم النصير" (and excellent is the Helper): i.e., He, exalted is He, is the excellent Helper, the one who gives you support.

Meaning of the verses:

After establishing the creed in its three parts: monotheism, prophethood, and resurrection with recompense, the Lord, blessed and exalted, addressed the Muslims with the title of faith, saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, i.e., you who have believed in Allah as Lord, in Muhammad as Messenger, and in Islam as religion. ﴿Bow and prostrate﴾, He commanded them to establish the prayer. ﴿And worship your Lord﴾, i.e., obey Him in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you, venerating Him with the utmost veneration and humbling yourselves before Him with the utmost humility. ﴿And do good﴾, of all that Allah has urged you to and encouraged you towards of kinds of righteousness and forms of worship. ﴿So that you may be successful﴾, i.e., so that you may qualify thereby for success, which is the winning of Paradise after salvation from the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾: i.e., He also commanded them with a matter of great importance, which is fighting the disbelievers until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah. The meaning of "striving due to Him" is as it should be, exerting all effort and capacity: with the self, with wealth, and with the call. And His saying: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾: this is a favour by which Allah, exalted is He, reminds the believers so that they may thank Allah by doing what He has commanded them. I.e., He did not constrict you in what He has commanded you, but made it expansive: He made repentance available for every sin, made expiation for some sins, granted the traveller and the sick concessions in shortening the prayer and fasting, and for one who does not find water or is unable to use it, tayammum.

And His saying: ﴿The religion of your father Abraham﴾: i.e., adhere to the religion of your father. And His saying: ﴿He named you Muslims﴾: i.e., Allah, majestic is His majesty, is the One who named them Muslims in the earlier scriptures and in the Qur'an, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿He named you Muslims before and in this﴾, i.e., the Qur'an. And His saying: ﴿That the Messenger may be a witness over you and that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾: i.e., He chose you, O believers, for His Islamic religion and named you Muslims, so that the Messenger may be a witness over you on the Day of Resurrection that he has conveyed to you what he was sent with, and you will be witnesses then over all the messengers that they conveyed to their peoples what they were sent with. Accordingly, thank Allah, the Exalted, for this blessing and honour. ﴿So establish the prayer, give the zakah, and hold fast to Allah﴾: i.e., hold firmly to His law in creed, worship, character, conduct, judgement and rule. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He is your Protector﴾: i.e., your Master and the Owner of your affairs. ﴿How excellent a Protector﴾: He, glorified and exalted is He. ﴿And how excellent a Helper﴾: i.e., the Helper for you as long as you are His allies, living in faith and piety.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The virtue of prayer, the nobility of worship, and the doing of good.

2- The legislation of prostration upon recitation of this verse: ﴿And do good, that you may be successful﴾.

3- The merit of striving in the way of Allah, which is fighting the disbelievers, and that the blame of any blamer should not deter the believer in Allah.

4- The virtue of this Muslim community, as it has been given three things that were given to no prophet except one. It was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Go, for there is no hardship upon you," and Allah said to this community: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾. It was said to the Prophet, peace be upon him: "You are a witness over your people," and Allah said: ﴿And that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾. It was said to the Prophet: "Ask and you will be given," and Allah said to this community: ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60]. This is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾.

5- The obligation of prayer and zakah, and adherence to the Shari'ah.
